newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreigner killed in deadly China train crash.
newsitem.headline: Foreigner killed in deadly China train crash.

text.p: One foreigner was among an estimated 100 people who died in a train crash in China's central Hunan province, one of the deadliest in China for several years, officials said on Friday.

Rescue workers trying to identify those killed on Tuesday when a passenger train ploughed into a stationary train in central China had found a body of a person who they believed was not Chinese, a provincial official said.

"We have reports that the body of a person with yellow hair and a high-bridged nose has been found, and we believe that this is a foreigner. But we do not yet know the nationality of this person," the official said.
The body carried no identification papers and the luggage of the dead person had yet to be found, the official said.
A provincial police officer said the dead foreigner was a man, but no other details were available.
Officials have placed the death toll from the crash at Rongjiawan station in Yueyang county at more than 100 with more than 300 injured, some of them seriously.

More than 3,000 people were on board the two trains at the time of the crash. The casualties included travellers waiting at the station who were hit by railway carriages pushed up onto the platform under the force of the collision, officials said.
Government officials handling rescue work have declined to give an exact toll from the crash, one of the worst in China for several years, saying this was a state secret.

The crowded No 324 passenger train, travelling north on the main trunk line between Beijing and the southern boomtown of Guangzhou, crashed into the back of the stationary No 818 on Tuesday, a Yueyang government official said.
Officials were investigating the cause of the crash, but initial reports showed human error and a failure to switch the points for the Kunming train might have been to blame.
